pairs.subject: candidate-self-scheduling
pairs.evidence: app/schedule/[token]/page.tsx:40 The booking page introduces the round with "Choose the slot that works best…". It never says what format the round takes and never asks about adjustments, and the escape hatch, time-zone and withdraw surfaces each fall short of their techniques.

techniques.evidence: app/schedule/[token]/page.tsx:40 Grepping adjustment/accommodat in app/schedule and the schedule catalog keys finds no ask, no field and no route. Only the duration is stated.

app/schedule/[token]/SlotPicker.tsx:106 Slots render only in the candidate's zone ("All times shown in your timezone"), with a short zone label. The anchor (interviewer) zone is never shown beside them, so the dual render is missing. Only ProposeSection names interviewTz.

app/schedule/[token]/SlotPicker.tsx:101 The hatch renders only once the horizon is empty or the cap is hit, not on the picker itself. The form is limited to 3 weekday times inside working hours (08:00-18:00) and has no free-text constraint, which the technique names as its failure.

app/schedule/[token]/SlotPicker.tsx:123 The display label is re-derived from the ISO instant in the reader's locale, with the server label as fallback. The client still posts slot: s.label (use-schedule-invite.ts:132), but the server ignores it.

app/schedule/[token]/use-schedule-invite.ts:189 Only a 409 (taken) refreshes the grid. A 400 SCHEDULE_SLOT_NOT_OFFERED, e.g. from a stale tab whose slot has passed, leaves an error banner over the stale list instead of "here are the current options".

pairs.subject: candidate-self-scheduling
pairs.evidence: app/api/schedule/[token]/route.ts:283 The token route refuses a candidate's proposal while any offered slot remains, and validateProposedSlots limits proposals to weekday business hours inside the horizon. That re-imposes the grid on the escape hatch, even though slot labels and structural validation are done right.

techniques.evidence: app/api/schedule/[token]/route.ts:354 body.slot is ignored. The label is minted from the validated instant for confirm and reschedule alike, and proposals are re-labelled server-side as well.

app/api/schedule/[token]/route.ts:350 Dead-link state checks run first (line 227). offeredSlotFor checks the slot is in the future, inside the horizon, on a weekday in the anchor zone, on one of TIMES, and at the exact canonical instant. A calendar race gets its own 409 with a re-offer, and a re-confirm is idempotent (line 321). Caveat: this is a predicate over TIMES, not membership in the freshly generated grid (the code says so), so it accepts structurally valid slots beyond the 6 actually shown.

app/api/schedule/route.ts:366 The bypass works: the recruiter path skips the cap and charges nothing, a same-slot pick is a no-op, and the count is taken inside the transaction. But the recruiter reschedule seals no actor/previous-slot record (cancel and no_show do), candidate reschedules log nothing either, the cap is the global MAX_RESCHEDULES=3 rather than a per-invitation value, and the race-lost SCHEDULE_RESCHEDULE_LIMIT refusal carries no proposal route.

app/api/schedule/[token]/route.ts:283 Proposals are allowed only at the two dead-ends, and proposedSlotFor rejects evenings, weekends and anything past the horizon (PROPOSAL_HOURS 8-18). There is no free-text field. The technique names this narrowness as its failure. On the plus side, a proposal restarts the expiry clock and a decline is recorded.

app/api/schedule/route.ts:307 The recruiter's company-side cancel reuses the candidate's RSVP primitive, so both leave attendance_status='cancelled' with no actor on the invite row (only a sealed decision for linked entries). Candidate withdraw ('declined') is distinct but terminal and irreversible, and no reason is stored.

app/_lib/schedule-slots.ts:130 Generation and validation reckon in one named IANA zone, and the candidate tz is captured. But that zone is deployment-wide, not stored on the invitation or beside the booking. The DST gap or overlap is not handled explicitly, and the validator is a separate predicate rather than the shared generator.

app/api/schedule/[token]/route.ts:48 The public projection and the POST body (slot/rsvp/withdraw/propose) carry no round-format description and no adjustment request. Nothing lets a candidate need change the slot length or format.

pairs.evidence: app/features/hiring/pipeline/PipelineTimelineItemRow.tsx:32 The recruiter timeline renders the stored slot column (an English, interviewer-zone label with no zone marker) inside a localized row, instead of deriving the label from slot_at in the reader's language.

techniques.evidence: app/features/hiring/pipeline/PipelineTimelineItemRow.tsx:32 candidate-timeline.ts:299 passes invite.slot (the cached column) through. The decision rule is "give it the derivation, not the column", and the localization section says to compose the label at render. The label is server-authored, so this is not an injection.

app/features/hiring/pipeline/PipelineTimelineItemRow.tsx:35 The timeline keeps separate facts: declined ("Interview declined by the candidate"), no_show and expired. A recruiter cancel is not shown as its own fact, because it returns the invite to pending.
